It was played by 12 teams. The national champion was [[Alianza Lima]].[https://historialblanquiazul.com/temporada-2001/ Alianza Temporada 2001][https://elcomercio.pe/deporte-total/futbol-peruano/alianza-lima-recordo-su-titulo-del-2001-del-ano-de-su-centenario-20-anos-de-ese-gran-momento-liga-1-cienciano-nczd-noticia/ Alianza Lima recordó el título que logró en su centenario: “20 años de ese gran momento”][https://depor.com/futbol-peruano/descentralizado/alianza-lima-campeon-2001-bernabe-herraez-entrenador-europeo-ganar-titulo-peru-57969/ Alianza Lima campeón 2001: Bernabé Herráez, el último entrenador europeo en ganar el título en Perú] == Competition format == The national championship was divided into two half-year tournaments, the [[Apertura and Clausura|Torneo Apertura]] and the [[Apertura and Clausura|Torneo Clausura]]. Each was played on a home-and-away [[Round-robin tournament|round-robin]] basis. The winners of each tournament played for the national title in a two-legged final. If the same team won both tournaments, they would be automatic champions. Qualification to CONMEBOL's [[Copa Libertadores]] was won by each tournament winner and the winner of a play-off between the teams that placed second in each tournament. The bottom team on the aggregate table was relegated, while the eleventh-placed team played a relegation/promotion play-off against the winner of the Segunda División (Second Division). == Teams == ===Team changes=== {| class="wikitable" |- !
